doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: George Lewis's early jobs and own band; Rene stays with his brother's band
summary: Lewis played with Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly and Kid Howard before forming his own band. Rene declined an offer to join him and stayed with his brother until work dried up in the 1930s.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: He went with different fellas and played music. He played with Sam Morgan, some. He played a few jobs with us, you know. And he played with Chris Kellys. Oh, yeah, that's about. Then he formed up his own band. Yeah. Formed off the board. George Lewis band. He got, first he had, oh no, he played with Kid Howard. Yes. Remember Kid Howard? Yes. Yeah, well, he played with him. But when he got out from Kid Howard, that way he formed his own band. He got this fella, Slowdrag, you know what you talking about? He played bass and he got this Jim Crow, what they call Jim Robinson. He played the trambone and he got there. And let's see who he got. He had another fella. Oh, Moreira on Band. Right. Lawrence. Lawrence. Lawrence.

And that's John Forkartin. Who was drumming with him? Well, he had, of course in the late years he had Joe Watkins. Who? Joe Watkins. Joe Watkins. Well, he was a much more recent drummer. You probably don't even remember him. Yeah, no. He died fairly recently.

Yeah, yeah. Well, there's another fella. I can't think of his name. He had a drummer. He tried to get me with him and I said, no, I wouldn't. I was going to leave my brother, you know. We had such, you know, good, wonderful band. I guess you must have heard.
I talked about it. Did you stay more or less continually playing with your brother all the time?
Yeah. Yeah. I continued. Then after we just couldn't get no work, things went bad, you know. Then we dissolved the band. That was when?
